summary: P3E17 opt-in background content-health reconciliation and bounded multi-route session bootstrap, without hidden source repair or shared publication.
scope: Server-owned local routes with existing explicit active generations. No consumer installation, UI, MCP, remote source export, arbitrary repository discovery or automatic compaction. Journal epochs/asynchronous capture remain separate debts; this user-prioritized content-health slice does not claim to close them.
routeInventory: GET /api/v1/projects/{project}/knowledge-routes authorizes through the existing project registry and returns configured route/workspace/source-host/profile IDs and monitored flags. No root paths, implicit attachment, health scan or readiness claim. Together with existing authorized project pagination, this lets a new client choose explicit bootstrap members.
policy: Required knowledge config: enabled, principal_id, route_ids, interval_seconds, max_age_seconds, prepare_on_drift. Disabled requires empty principal/routes and no preparation. Enabled binds a configured admin and1..8 unique configured routes. Intervals1..3600 seconds; age1..86400 and at least interval. Target count fits resident generation slots and worst-case payload reservation. prepare_on_drift requires the preparation worker. All authority is attached explicitly at configuration time, not granted by a GET.
background: One cooperative std::jthread, immediate startup pass, bounded round-robin targets and periodic checks. No overlapping checks. Foreground activity postpones admission; an already running Core scan is not preempted and Core retains its own bounded parallelism. This is admission preference, not a hard CPU reservation or liveness/latency SLO under saturation. Uses the same active-artifact ownership and resident cache as foreground retrieval. Health is process-local and lost on restart; startup must reacquire evidence. Service alive, cached health, exact-current content and context-ready remain independent. Coalesced_requests counts target refresh hints, not outer HTTP requests.
assessment: Native read-only vacuum compares canonical generated output, reports counts and expected snapshot identity. Doctor, profile and configured eval/Pack suites are separate checks; final exact source/artifact/route verification bounds the observation. Bootstrap-only profiles explicitly mark project quality not-configured rather than invent passing suites. No source, active generation, publication or journal mutation during assessment; no test/build shell is executed.
preparation: Only prepare_on_drift policy may enqueue an ordinary bounded preparation for a changed canonical snapshot. Key binds route fingerprint, active revision and expected generated identity; retries deduplicate. Existing job quotas and publication CAS remain authoritative. A candidate is never automatically activated or offered as current context. Source may change while the candidate builds; normal preflight/activation must still verify it.
retry: A terminal failed/cancelled automatic candidate is not recreated indefinitely for the same identity. maintenance_action.next_action directs explicit review/reprepare using the existing preparation API with a fresh reviewed idempotency key, or a changed source/base identity produces a new automatic key. No automatic retry epoch is installed. If enqueue completion is uncertain, mutations_performed is null and completion_uncertain is explicit; never claim no mutation after an ambiguous commit.
healthRead: GET /api/v1/projects/{project}/routes/{route}/knowledge-health authorizes against Store, checks configured route/workspace and compares active selection identity. It returns cached metadata with age, expiry and selection alignment, not a new scan. A previous healthy assessment is not exact-current proof at read time. TTL uses steady_clock from assessment start, conservatively including scan duration. index_current covers exact profile-owned source/generated-output agreement, not all repository files; false does not alone prove a source edit. Unmonitored, pending, expired, changed, unhealthy and unavailable states are explicit.
maintenanceApi: GET /api/v1/knowledge-maintenance is admin-only process status/counters. POST /api/v1/knowledge-maintenance/refresh accepts an empty object and coalesces a rescan request; it neither blocks for completion nor grants new target authority. Ordinary reads never request maintenance.
bootstrapRequest: POST /api/v1/session-bootstrap: exact object task_id (opaque ASCII identifier1..128), members (1..8), max_evidence_bytes (1024..131072). Each member is exact project_id, route_id, query (1..2048 bytes), required (boolean). Duplicate project/route pairs rejected; at least one required. Every member is authorized before any retrieval, including optional members. Membership is caller-reviewed, not inferred from cwd or product nouns.
bootstrapResult: shin.session-bootstrap.v1: task_id, ready, context_ready, health_ready, members, evidence_bytes, max_evidence_bytes, read_only=true. Required members processed before optional members, preserving input order within each class. Each context uses ordinary exact-current compact Brief (limit4), keeps its canonical envelope and provenance, and is retained whole or explicitly budget-exceeded. No cross-profile scoring or merged index. Required empty evidence or uncovered query groups prevents context_ready. Retrieval and health are independent: reason_code and health_reason_code preserve each failure without erasing the other successful result. Missing optional evidence yields a visible partial result; required context or health gaps prevent ready. HTTP success means assessment completed, not ready=true. This local-route bootstrap does not select shared publication heads implicitly.
resourceBoundary: At most8 members,131072 retained context bytes and262144 response bytes. Member accumulation is checked incrementally. This is not a total RSS bound: callbacks are bounded existing service methods, retrieval independently limits each response to512KiB and scheduler assessment metadata to16KiB, and native generation/snapshot limits remain separate. No arbitrary unbounded callback is supplied by HTTP clients.
continuity: Bootstrap is stateless orientation for a new or continuing task, not a chat store, checkpoint adoption or resume replacement. Existing Core checkpoint/resume retains explicit project/task/thread/TTL checks. Multi-member snapshots are independently observed; no distributed source-time transaction is claimed. Caller must verify task-specific source paths and uncovered query groups.
vacuumBoundary: Never run vacuum --apply against an active immutable candidate. Content drift produces findings and optionally a new preparation. Physical removal of old generations/history remains explicit existing plan/apply with pins and receipts. PostgreSQL autovacuum is unrelated to this content-health contract.
sourceUse: Controller reconciliation and cooperative thread lifetime are architectural references, not new runtime dependencies or an exactly-once/real-time claim.
